A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same frequency-filtering research, despite the changed title and template. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching.

before.justification: v2 reports original membership-inference experiments on DDIM and Stable Diffusion, including benchmark results, ablations, and defense evaluations.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds standard-setting CLID results and an adaptive-defense evaluation.

M1.justification: The proposed attack filter and scoring procedure in Equations 9–11 remain unchanged. Section 5.6 adds a proposed adaptive defense that suppresses low-frequency amplitudes and injects noise during fine-tuning, constituting a limited new procedure.

E1.justification: Table 1 switches the failed-sample analysis from STL10-U to CIFAR-100, although both remain in the overall benchmark suite. v3 also evaluates Pokémon under a frequency-targeted adaptive defense. The existing datasets, modalities, and caption-access scenarios are otherwise retained.

E2.justification: v3 adds CLID and CLID+F to the typical strong-overfitting comparison in Table 12. v2 evaluated CLID only under weak overfitting, whose results are retained as v3 Table 13. Naive, SecMI, and PIA remain the principal comparators.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 changes the reported frequency-analysis boundary from radius 5 generally to radius 2 for CIFAR-100 and Tiny-IN. Added evaluations cover CLID under typical overfitting and adaptive-defense fine-tuning with 70–90% low-frequency amplitudes and noise variance 0.05. Existing splits, training budgets, and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5.6 and Appendix D.10 add a targeted robustness test asking whether perturbing low-frequency training information reduces the filter's advantage. Table 1 revises the failed-sample analysis, and existing parameter sweeps receive numerical revisions. The logarithmic ROC panels primarily redisplay existing results.

E5.justification: The Kolmogorov–Smirnov tests, significance threshold, and score-distribution statistics are retained. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or uncertainty estimates for attack performance.

E6.justification: v3 adds typical-setting CLID results and adaptive-defense results, and revises Table 1 statistics. Existing ablation values also change: MS-COCO ASR at r_t=5, s=0.1 changes from 94.59 to 93.59; Tiny-IN ASR/AUC at that setting changes from 85.13/92.28 to 84.91/92.18. These are revised reported values without an explanation of their provenance. Main benchmark Tables 2, 3, and 5 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix C recasts the proof as a forward sufficient-condition argument, replacing v2's if-and-only-if step and removing covariance terms under independence. The proposition also explicitly mentions an existing membership advantage. Its principal inequality and the attack-equivalence derivations in Appendix B remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: a unified error-based attack framework, high-frequency deficiency analysis, and a broadly applicable filter with negligible overhead. The new title and supporting experiments do not materially redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v3 explains the adaptive defense through reduced low-frequency overfitting and acknowledges possible degradation of generation quality, which is not measured. Appendix D.5 qualifies the gains when CLID already performs exceptionally well, and D.8 adds a cross-resolution hyperparameter-generality argument. The pre-training limitation is retained through relocation.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies that baseline threshold-acquisition procedures follow the original publications and documents adaptive-defense parameters. Hardware, training settings, and code-release statements are retained. New prose in Sections 5.4 and D.8 reverses s and r_t, conflicting with the unchanged implementation settings s=0.2 and r_t=5.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a dedicated frequency-analysis discussion, including new citations to Rissanen et al. (2022), Yi et al. (2024), and Zhang et al. (2024b). It expands the spectral-bias context while retaining the existing membership-inference positioning and novelty claim.

P1.justification: The title and several headings change, with localized prose edits and added explanations. Limitations move from the conclusion to Appendix E, and later experimental appendices are reordered. Most existing narrative remains substantially intact.

P2.justification: The main text changes from one column to two columns, with extensive display reflow. Figures 1 and 2 become two-by-two grids; Figure 7 is rearranged and its parameter-axis labels corrected. Figure 8 adds six logarithmic ROC panels, two result tables are added, and Table 6 is condensed to baseline scores and gains.

improvement.justification: The adaptive-defense test probes a previously untested weakness, while standard-setting CLID results improve assessment of applicability beyond the earlier weak-overfitting comparison. These provide a modest improvement in evidential completeness and qualification of the method's benefits. The gains outweigh localized reporting regressions, particularly reversed hyperparameter names and unexplained ablation-value revisions, but do not establish a substantial overall improvement.
